cards.name: Spruce log to slab mega farm (underground autocrafter, sell axe AFK)
cards.source: videos/L5oVTgYM4Zg.txt - Bubsy, uploaded 2026-08-28 (spruce slab mega farm)
cards.claimed_gross_per_hour: '$200 million an hour' at full fill ('almost 300,000 slabs every minute' x $12); '5 billion every day' at the end of the video, 'over 3 billion a day' earlier in the same video; 1-hour AFK test: 'made 198 million, and it wasn't even fully filled' (balance delta while running, logs already paid for)
cards.claimed_profit_per_hour: Not stated per hour. Video states 'over $20 profit per log'. Derived (not in video): 1 log = 4 planks = 8 slabs = $96 at base price vs 72-74 per log on /orders = $22-24 per log; at the stated full-fill rate (4,680 slabs/s = ~585 logs/s = ~2.1M logs/h) net is roughly $46-50M/h, so the $200M/h and 5B/day figures are gross before ~$155M/h of log cost.
cards.capital_required: Drill 195M on /ah (used for digging); sell axe 24M for 18 hours remaining on /ah; log float 74M per 1M logs; crafters, hoppers, chests and ice for a farm holding 10-11M logs (not priced); golden carrot stack from /ah
cards.setup_time: About 5 days ('I've been doing this video for 5 days') with teammates digging and placing chest layers; Bubsy's Discord builder team sells the build delivered in under 48 hours

inputs.qty: 1,000,000 ordered in one order, plus 'two pages of logs' already held; farm holds 10-11M
inputs.unit_price: 74 (order: '$74 million for a million logs'); highest existing buy order was 72.1
24M for a listing with 18 hours left

outputs.qty: '4,68 slabs every second' (likely 4,680/s), 'almost 300,000 slabs every minute' at full fill
outputs.unit_price: $12 each, '$768' per stack (base price via sell axe)

cards.process: 1) Chain per line: input chest -> hoppers -> crafter with planks recipe -> hopper -> crafter with slab recipe; crafters are pulsed by a redstone clock; a note block / lever power switch with an indicator lamp shows whether the clock runs. 2) Tested with two stacks of spruce bought on /ah, then scaled to many crafters fed from one input chest by a hopper distribution system so all crafters fill themselves. 3) Dug a large underground room with the 3x3 drill (195M on /ah); bottom layer is ice, then layers that are almost 100% chests for slab storage, plus an AFK area with a water stream. 4) Buy logs by placing /orders spruce log above the highest existing order (72.1 -> 74; 1M logs for 74M), open the order and drop the delivered logs into the input hopper. 5) Turn the farm on; slabs flow down and fill the chest layers ('each stack of slabs is $768'). 6) Cash out AFK: buy a sell axe on /ah (sells a chest's contents at base price instead of breaking it, self-destructs 24h after purchase), golden carrots in the off hand, Options > Controls: sneak = toggle, attack/destroy = toggle, use item/place block = toggle; click the note block to start, walk into the water stream, crouch once, look straight up, right click once, left click once, wear no armor. The stream cycles you past the chests while the sell axe keeps selling.
tricks: Beat the highest existing buy order by a small margin to get logs delivered (72.1 -> 74)
Place a single 1,000,000-log order at 74 ($74M); farm storage takes 10-11M logs
Sell axe from /ah: pick the listing with the most time left (24M for 18 hours); it self-destructs 24 hours after purchase
AFK toggle setup: golden carrots in off hand, Options > Controls: sneak, attack/destroy, use item/place block all set to toggle; crouch once, look straight up, right click once, left click once
No armor while AFKing: 'otherwise it'll break the water flow'
Note block / lever power switch wired to a lamp so you can see whether the clock is running
Hopper distribution system so every crafter fills from one input chest
Bottom layer of the farm is ice
Pick good coordinates and fill in caves so the base is not found (builder team does this)
Expect a few pressure plates and buttons to be crafted on first start from partial grids; it stops once the crafters are full
Check whether you were raided on login before continuing to build
Buy a 3x3 drill on /ah to dig the room (195M)
quotes: if you just chop down a spruce tree, craft all of the logs into planks, and then craft all those planks into slabs, you make an insane amount of profit
195 mil. Let's buy that one. And if you guys don't know what this does, and it breaks nine blocks at once.
slash orders spruce log. And then you try and beat out the highest one. So this one's 72.1.
This farm can hold up to 10 million logs. And this farm makes over 3 billion a day.
Each stack of slabs is $768, which means you're making over $20 profit per log.
ah sell axe. And this axe, whenever you mine a chest, it actually doesn't mine it, but instead sells everything in it.
They self-destruct after 24 hours. So, I'm going to find a good one. This one's pretty good. 24 mil for 18 hours.
we're going to make this order for $74 million for a million logs
you guys cannot have any armor on otherwise it'll break the water flow
AFK for that 1 hour made 198 million, and it wasn't even fully filled

The farm can hold almost 11 million logs. And when it's fully filled, it makes 4,68 slabs every second, which means almost 300,000 slabs every minute. With slabs being $12 per, this farm makes $200 million an hour or 5 billion every day.
There's nothing else being crafted except for a couple pressure plates and buttons whenever we first started it.
for a small price, our builder team will build it for you in less than 48 hours at good coordinates and fill in all the caves for you
cards.risks: Gross and profit are conflated: $200M/h is slab revenue at $12 before ~74/log input cost; the video's own 'over $20 profit per log' implies net around a quarter of that. Two daily figures given (over 3B vs 5B). Sell axe expires 24h after purchase, so an idle day wastes ~24M. Base discovery and raids (teammate joked about seeing a nametag through the wall / X-ray). Log supply: a farm eating ~2M logs/h will move the /orders price. Crafters make junk (buttons, pressure plates) when partially filled. Armor breaks the water AFK loop. Lag at thousands of crafts per second.
cards.scalability: Bounded by spruce log supply on /orders (full fill needs ~2.1M logs/h; the creator had 1M plus two pages), sell axe cost and 24h timer (one axe per day), crafter and hopper counts (block limits), and drill cost for digging. Output sells to the server at base price, so AH slots do not matter.

cards.process: Bone blocks go into the top chests -> flow down to a crafter that turns them into bone meal ('once it overfills, it'll detect it and stop crafting') -> bone meal is distributed to dispensers -> dispensers bone meal the kelp -> pistons break the grown kelp -> water carries the kelp to the collection end. A button toggles the farm on/off. Recommended add-ons: an auto smelter and an autocrafter after the collection point (dried kelp -> dried kelp blocks). Bubsy overfilled with bone meal and it spilled out.
tricks: Put an auto smelter and an autocrafter after the collection point to turn kelp into dried kelp blocks
The bone meal crafter stops when the output overfills, so bone meal does not clog the line
Button start/stop
Speed tested in a test world by raising tick speed (not possible on the server)
quotes: in about a minute's time, we've made 600 kelp
I set the tick speed to speed it up and we're going to see how much I made in about an hour... 2,34. That is a full inventory.

And it'll go through all of these and go into the dispensers. And the dispenser will spit out bone meal onto the kelp. And once the kelp grows, the pistons break and it goes down the water all the way to the end.

cards.name: Log to plank to chest crafter farm with shulker loader (Tomax chest crafter, Melton expansion) - sold into chest buy orders
cards.claimed_gross_per_hour: Tomax's original: 'This makes 750 million dollars an hour' (also said to make 'only' 'around 100 mil an hour'); Melton's 5-minute test: chests valued at '$10 million' (at $200 per chest), 'not even half capacity', scaled x6 and x12 = '720 million dollars' per hour; 'with mine you can make up to 400 million dollars an hour profit'
cards.claimed_profit_per_hour: 'about 3 to 400 million dollars an hour of profit' ('half of this is not profit'); with the realistic hourly operating cycle 'around 300 mil of profit an hour'
cards.capital_required: Drill 20M on /ah (March 2026); 256 crafters plus hoppers and cyan stained glass ordered on /orders; shulker boxes ordered at 850 each; log float (spent 200M on a log order by mistake); schematic free in the description
cards.setup_time: Many days: full schematic build, plank-stage expansion (4 crafters stacked per column), water streams, soul sand water elevator, shulker loader expanded to ~20 ('That took an hour' alone)

inputs.qty: 'like 500k' loaded to reach max capacity; 2 logs per chest

outputs.qty: 'around half a million planks' from 25 s of plank crafting (= ~62.5k chests); ~21,000 planks/s at max capacity

cards.process: Stage 1 (Melton's addition): logs dropped into the input; crafters stacked 4 high craft logs -> planks; planks ride two water streams (plus a soul sand water elevator) into the chest farm. Stage 2 (Tomax's chest crafter): planks -> chests (8 planks = 2 logs per chest). Stage 3: chests pass through a shulker loader (expanded to ~20 loaders) into shulker boxes, which go to a storage/control room. Sell the chests by filling player buy orders on /orders (chest $200, normally $400). The clock had to be slowed because a too-fast clock made the crafters produce buttons from partial grids and lost money. Max capacity ~21,000 planks/s needs ~500k logs loaded. Hourly operating cycle: fill with logs, run the plank crafters 15 s, turn on the chest crafters, wait until the planks are gone, turn the plank stage off, then the chest stage off, check the shulker loader, repeat.
tricks: Buy logs and craft planks yourself: 'planks are so high on orders, and logs are way lower. And plus, planks take way longer to get delivered'
Slow the clock when crafters start making buttons (partial recipe from a clock faster than the hoppers)
Size the shulker loader to the chest rate (expanded to about 20)
Stack 4 crafters per column for the plank stage
Soul sand water elevator to move items up; two parallel water streams feed the chest stage
Order shulkers slightly above market (800 -> 850) to get filled
Order 256 crafters, hoppers and stained glass on /orders instead of buying on /ah
Read the recipe before ordering (ordered logs instead of planks, 'wasted 200 mil', which led to the log->plank stage)
Use the drill to clear whole layers (20M)
Run in bursts: 15 s of planks, then chests, then check the loader, repeat every hour

cards.process: Buy sand and gravel, craft concrete powder with dye, harden it in water, mine the concrete, sell finished concrete. Choose the color the current farm schematic or meta uses.
tricks: Most players skip the hardening step ('too lazy to actually process the concrete'); doing that one extra step captures the spread
When a new schematic or farm meta uses a specific concrete color, that color spikes instantly to 90-100k per stack; be stocked before others react
Price depends heavily on color
quotes: The absolute cheapest colors can go for around 60k per stack, but that's pretty rare. Most of the time you're selling between 70 and 90k, usually around 80k per stack.
Every time a new farm meta drops, or someone releases a schematic, and that build uses a specific concrete color, that color spikes instantly.
when that happens, you can sell for 90k, sometimes even 100k per stack
cards.risks: Color-specific demand; listings capped by AH slots (18 default); pre-update prices
cards.scalability: 18 AH slots or buy-order depth per color; sand and gravel supply

cards.name: Piglin bartering (gold blocks to ingots, sell lever and blackstone)
cards.claimed_gross_per_hour: 1 million in gold blocks -> 'more than quadrupled my money' in about 20 minutes; worst runs 'still doubled the money'
cards.claimed_profit_per_hour: not stated per hour; derived: +3M on 1M in ~20 minutes on the lucky run (~9M/h), +1M on 1M worst case
cards.setup_time: a piglin pen in the nether; 'More piglins, faster trades'
cards.process: Buy gold blocks, craft them into ingots, barter with piglins, sort the loot into chests, sell lever and blackstone (soul sand, gravel and spectral arrows as bonus).
tricks: Lever and blackstone carry the whole method; everything else is bonus
More gold and more piglins scale it: 'There's no hard cap. The only limit is how much gold you're willing to invest.'
quotes: two items carry this entire method, lever and blackstone. Lever sells for insane prices. Blackstone moves consistently.
I invested 1 million into gold blocks, traded all of it, sorted the loot into chests, and added up the values. That run more than quadrupled my money.
Even on my worst runs though, I still doubled the money.
What took me 20 minutes could theoretically happen in seconds, with a big enough setup
cards.risks: RNG ('I definitely got lucky on that run'); lever price is the whole edge and is unstated; pre-update; nether exposure
cards.scalability: 'infinitely scalable' per creator (gold supply, piglin count); resale limited by AH slots and order depth for lever and blackstone
cards.still_valid_after_june_2026_update: unknown - pre-update; lever, blackstone and gold block prices must be re-checked

cards.name: Villager librarian hall with 1-emerald book trades (zombify and cure), selling enchanted books
cards.claimed_gross_per_hour: 'the 2050 to 300 million per hour range' as transcribed (likely 250 to 300 million per hour); 'This is what got me to 1 billion.'
cards.claimed_profit_per_hour: per book: mending bought for 1 emerald sells 'for around 25k'; other books '70k or even 80k sometimes'
cards.capital_required: 2 zombie villagers to cure, a breeder, lecterns, a zombie, emeralds (source not stated)
cards.setup_time: hours to days: breed villagers, reroll lecterns until the book starts at 24 emeralds or less, zombify and cure each villager once
cards.process: Cure two zombie villagers, build a villager breeder, place and break lecterns until the librarian's book trade starts at 24 emeralds or less, build one long wall of villagers, keep one zombie at the back, zombify each villager once and cure it to lock the trade at 1 emerald, then walk down the line trading emeralds for books and sell the books.
tricks: Only trades with a base price of 24 emeralds or less drop to 1 emerald after one zombify and cure
20-30 villagers so that trade resets do not matter: 'You're always moving'
Build the trade set around what sells fast (mending is the most consistent)
quotes: breaking lecterns until you get books that start at 24 emeralds or less. Because that's the key. Once you zombie fire and cure a villager one time, the price drops to one emerald. But only if the base price is low enough.
Take mending as an example. You buy it for one emerald, and you can sell it for around 25k. And mending is stable.
that's how you end up in the 2050 to 300 million per hour range. Not in some perfect scenario, just with a solid setup and enough villagers.
Other books can go for 70k or even 80k sometimes, but those prices fluctuate more.
cards.risks: 250-300M/h at 25k-80k per book needs 3,000-12,000 books an hour, far beyond what 20-30 villagers can restock, so the hourly claim looks inflated. Emerald sourcing cost is not addressed. Listings are capped by AH slots (18 default); book demand fluctuates.
cards.scalability: Villager restock limits, villager count, AH slots (18 default), book demand
cards.still_valid_after_june_2026_update: unknown - pre-update; villager mechanics are untouched by the June update, but book prices and the AH slot cut to 18 matter
verification_items: whether the zombify/cure discount works on the server

mechanics_facts.fact: Autocrafter chain log -> planks -> slabs: crafter with planks recipe, hopper, crafter with slab recipe, all pulsed by a redstone clock behind a lever or note block power switch; a hopper distribution system fills every crafter from one input chest.

Crafters with partially filled grids craft unintended items (pressure plates and buttons at startup; buttons when the clock is faster than the hoppers). Fix: let crafters fill before clocking, or slow the clock.

Sell axe: bought with /ah sell axe; 'whenever you mine a chest, it actually doesn't mine it, but instead sells everything in it'; 'They self-destruct after 24 hours'; listings show remaining time (24 mil for 18 hours).
Drill (shard pickaxe) 'breaks nine blocks at once' (3x3), bought with /ah drill; 195M on 2026-08-28, 20M on 2026-03-22.
/orders fill tactic: bid just above the highest existing buy order (72.1 -> 74 on spruce logs; 73.5 -> 74 two weeks earlier). A 1,000,000-log order at 74 ($74M) was filled.

AFK sell-axe loop: golden carrots in the off hand (auto-eat), Options > Controls set sneak, attack/destroy and use item/place block to toggle; crouch once, look straight up, right click once, left click once; stand in a water stream under the output chests; no armor or the water flow breaks.
/worth spruce slab = 12 (base price); a stack of slabs is $768; 1 log = 8 slabs = $96, so 'over $20 profit per log' at a 72-74 log price.

Sell-axe area design: output chests above a water stream so the AFK player keeps breaking (selling) chests; used instead of a shulker loader because 'shulker prices will take away a good proportion of the profits'.
Cobblestone farms were nerfed before 2026-06-29; basalt was 'considered the meta' after that; basalt farms only run efficiently in the nether because lava flows faster there.
Bone economics on 2026-06-29: bones $90, so bone meal $30 (3 per bone); pink petals or wildflowers yield 60-70 per bone meal at base price ('over two times the profit per bone').
Pink petal farms 'used to be making like 60 million per hour' before a nerf (metas get nerfed).
Bone-meal flower farms produce pink petals in a cherry grove and wildflowers in a birch forest; biome sets the product.
Flower Bunker V2: 56 Flower Power V7 modules, ~900,000 bone storage, 50-60M/h gross, 30-40M/h net at $90 bones; lever with light (light off = producing).

IKEA V1 kelp farm (Mishkat): bone blocks -> crafter (stops when output overfills) -> dispensers -> kelp -> pistons -> water collection; ~600 kelp/min observed; add an auto smelter and autocrafter for dried kelp blocks.
Kelp farms claimed at 40M/h (pre-update); Bubsy on 2026-08-28 says most people think the meta is dried kelp blocks or cobblestone.
Chest crafter economics (March 2026): 8 planks = 2 logs per chest; chests sell into /orders at $200 ('normally $400'); chests are shulker-loaded before selling.
Planks are priced much higher than logs on /orders and plank orders take far longer to fill, so buy logs and craft planks in-farm.
An /orders entry for crafters showed '1 day 18 hours' remaining in March 2026 (order lifetime appeared longer than 24h pre-update).

Melton's plank stage: ~21,000 planks/s at max capacity, which needs ~500k logs loaded; 25 s of crafting made ~500k planks; the shulker loader had to be expanded to ~20 to keep up; the farm lagged an RTX 3080 client.
Shulker boxes were ordered on /orders at 850 with the market at 800 (March 2026).
Concrete prices by color: 60k/stack cheapest (rare), 70-90k typical (~80k), 90-100k for the color the current schematic/meta uses; the meta color spikes instantly when a schematic drops.
Piglin bartering: lever and blackstone are the profitable drops; 1M of gold blocks more than quadrupled in ~20 minutes on a lucky run, worst runs doubled.
Villager discount: reroll lecterns until the book trade starts at 24 emeralds or less; zombify and cure once and the price drops to 1 emerald; mending sells ~25k, other books 70-80k.
Sand insta-mined with an Efficiency III shovel and sold with /sell made 240,000 in about 2 minutes (pre-update).
Hand-chopping spruce made 'around 50,000 dollars' in 1 minute (pre-update, channel not stated); the Board tree farm makes spruce logs AFK but needs two accounts.
Crafters crafting crafters returned 1.1M on ~800k of ingredients in a small test build (pre-update).
Base opsec: an amethyst cluster near a base can reveal it; destroy the budding amethyst so clusters cannot regrow, and /sell the amethyst.
Builder services exist: Bubsy's Discord #ordfarm builds a farm in under 48 hours at good coordinates with caves filled; SadBonker's Discord offers a building service and skeleton spawner trading.

Bubsy mega farm: bottom layer is ice; storage layers are almost 100% chests; capacity stated as 'up to 10 million logs' and 'almost 11 million logs'; daily figure stated both as 'over 3 billion a day' and '5 billion every day'.

Melton's max-capacity operating cycle: fill with logs, plank crafters on for 15 s, then chest crafters on, wait for planks to run out, plank stage off, chest stage off, check shulker loader, repeat hourly for ~300M/h profit (claimed).
